summary: This is a JUnit test class for a TrafficLight object. Each test creates a fresh light, advances it through the Red \u2192 Green \u2192 Yellow \u2192 Red cycle, and checks both the current colour and whether drivers must stop.

lines.text: Brings in the @Test annotation from JUnit 5, which is how the test runner recognises a method as a test to execute.
A static import lets you write assertEquals(...) directly instead of Assertions.assertEquals(...), which keeps the test bodies readable.
The test class is named after the class under test, a convention that makes the pairing obvious to both readers and tools.
Test method names describe the behaviour being verified, so a failure report reads like a sentence about what broke.
Every test builds its own light, so no test can be affected by changes another test made.
Checks the expected value against the actual one; in JUnit the expected value always comes first.
Asserts that a boolean is true, documenting that a red light must stop traffic.
The single call under test is separated from the setup above by a blank line, following the arrange-act-assert shape.
Green is the one state where stopping is not required, so this test pins down the negative case too.
Advancing three times should wrap back to Red, which proves the cycle loops rather than running off the end.
